title: QVF Manifest
description: Canonical JSON Schema for manifest.json inside a .qvf archive (QVF format version 1). This file is the single source of truth for the QVF contract: where the specification prose and this schema disagree, the schema wins. The root thermochemistry, dipole_moment and constraints metadata blocks, the extensions governance block, and the per-section critical flag are optional additions within v1; archives that omit them remain valid. It also carries the payload definitions, the $defs entries whose names end in `Payload` (StructurePayload, JobSpecPayload, VolumeGridPayload, …), which specify the JSON payloads of archive members by section kind and role. Those payloads are separate archive members, so nothing in the manifest $refs them; a validator loads each member's bytes and checks them against the definition. See QVF spec § 5 (Canonical section kinds) and § 6 (Validation semantics).

qvf_version.description: QVF format version. v1 is the only released version.

schema_uri.description: Canonical URI of this JSON Schema. Informational; not validated against.

byte_order.description: Byte order of every binary member of the archive. The only valid value is 'little', which every v1 archive is whether or not it declares it; any other value is invalid. A later major version moves the byte order into the dtype names. See QVF spec § 2.2 (Endianness).

provenance.description: Optional calculation provenance carried at manifest root. Open: a key not listed here is allowed. See QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

hostname.description: Deprecated; see QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance). The name of the machine the calculation ran on. Producers SHOULD NOT emit it; consumers MUST ignore it for any purpose other than display and MUST NOT rely on it. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid; it may be removed in a future major version.

run_status.description: The archive's place in a calculation's lifecycle, as defined in QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance): 'pending' = a job described (structure + job.spec) but not yet run; 'running' = a live mid-run checkpoint snapshot; 'converged' / 'failed' = a settled terminal archive. Absent means 'not stated' — a consumer MUST NOT infer a status.

software.description: The programs and libraries that produced the results, one object per component: the program itself, the integral library it called, and so on. Each names the component and may give its version and its home page; see QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance). The root `source` names the QVF producer, and this list names every component that shaped the numbers.

git_commit.description: The producer's own source revision: a git commit hash of 7 to 64 hexadecimal characters, so an abbreviated hash, a 40-character SHA-1 or a 64-character SHA-256 hash. Git prints lowercase; see QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

n_threads.description: Number of threads the calculation ran with, per process; see QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

n_mpi_ranks.description: Number of MPI ranks (processes) the calculation ran with; 1 for a serial run. See QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

n_gpus.description: Number of GPUs the calculation used; 0 for a run that used none. See QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

started_utc.description: When the calculation started: an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ with an optional fractional second, e.g. '2026-10-07T12:00:00Z'; see QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

finished_utc.description: When the calculation finished, in the form of `started_utc`; see QVF spec § 3.2 (provenance).

metadata.description: Optional descriptive metadata of the archive as a whole: title, authors, licence, identifiers and time stamps; see QVF spec § 3.5 (Root metadata).

viewer_defaults.description: Hints for consumers that render the archive; see QVF spec § 3.4 (viewer_defaults). The members auto_open, bookmarks, camera and crossfade are reserved and no section may use one as its id; every other key is a section id whose value is that section's hint object.

bookmarks.description: Ordered camera bookmarks for consistent framing across viewers and movie export. The list order is the playback order.

camera.description: The camera a consumer starts with, an object in the shape of #/$defs/Camera. Specified in QVF spec § 3.4 (viewer_defaults) only: the schema does not check the value, so a malformed camera never makes an archive invalid, and a consumer ignores one it cannot use.

crossfade.description: Two scalar-field sections to cross-fade between and the initial position of the blend: {a, b, blend?}, where a and b are section ids and blend is a number from 0 to 1, default 0.5. Specified in QVF spec § 3.4 (viewer_defaults) only: the schema does not check the value, so a malformed cross-fade never makes an archive invalid, and a consumer ignores one it cannot use.

thermochemistry.description: Optional thermochemical corrections at manifest root; see QVF spec § 3.3 (Root metadata blocks).

dipole_moment.description: Optional dipole moment at manifest root; see QVF spec § 3.3 (Root metadata blocks).

constraints.description: Optional geometry optimisation constraints at manifest root; see QVF spec § 3.3 (Root metadata blocks).

energies.description: Optional energies of the calculation at manifest root: the energy of the primary result, its components, and energies by further methods; see QVF spec § 3.6 (Root energies).

extensions.description: Optional extension governance block declaring vendor extensions in use; see QVF spec § 7.4 (Root extensions block and per-section critical).

units.description: Unit of `value`: a unit name, or one of the legacy spellings that archives written before the vocabulary carry. Producers write the unit name; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

UnitName.description: A unit name of the QVF unit vocabulary, the controlled list of unit strings in QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions), which lists the same names in the same order with the quantity and definition of each. Names are case-sensitive. Every `units` object, `x_units`, `y_units` and `broadening.units` of a member payload, and the `units` of a {value, units} object, names its unit with one of these.

LegacyUnitName.description: Deprecated spellings that a {value, units} object (ValueWithUnits) still accepts, because archives written before the unit vocabulary carry them: `Eh` and `Hartree` mean `hartree`, `eV` means `ev`. Producers write the unit name instead; consumers read a legacy spelling as the unit it names. Nowhere else is a legacy spelling a unit name; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

Camera.description: VTK-flavoured camera. Position, focal point, and view-up are world-coordinate Cartesian (Å); the focal point is what the camera looks at, view_up is its roll axis. Projection is set by exactly one of view_angle (perspective, degrees) or parallel_scale (orthographic, world units).

ZipPath.description: Path of the member inside the zip archive. Forward slashes; no leading slash; no '..' segments.

MemberSize.description: Uncompressed byte count of the stored member: it must equal the uncompressed size the ZIP central directory records for the member's entry, which a validator checks before reading the member. Optional on every member spec. See QVF spec § 4.2 (Member specs).

MediaType.description: IANA media type of the member's bytes, a type and a subtype without parameters (RFC 6838), e.g. 'image/png' or 'text/plain'. Optional on every member spec; it describes the bytes and changes nothing in how they are read. A kind may require it, as `preview` does. See QVF spec § 4.2 (Member specs).

id.description: Unique identifier for this section within the file.

kind.description: Kind string from the QVF registry or x_<vendor>.* namespace.

critical.description: If true, a consumer that does not support this kind MUST refuse to open the archive; see QVF spec § 7.4 (Root extensions block and per-section critical).

structure_ref.description: Id of the `structure` section this section describes. It must name a section of kind `structure` in this archive. When one of the section's payloads also carries a `structure_ref` (the `basis` of a `wavefunction.gto`), this one takes precedence; see QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object).

run_ref.description: Id of the `run.record` section of the program run that produced this section. It must name a section of kind `run.record` in this archive; see QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object).

group.description: Free-text label that groups related sections for display, e.g. 'step 2: frequencies'. Sections with equal `group` values belong together; the value carries no other meaning; see QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object).

Volume4DVectorBinary.description: The `data` member of a `volume.vector` section: float32 or float64 [nx, ny, nz, 3], one Cartesian vector per grid point, the last axis holding its x, y and z components. That the leading three extents equal the grid `shape` is not checked by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

Volume4DComplexBinary.description: The `data` member of a `volume.complex` section: float32 or float64 [nx, ny, nz, 2], one complex value per grid point, the last axis holding [re, im] as for complex phonon eigenvectors. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

StructureAtom.description: One atom of a `structure` payload. `position` is Cartesian, in Ångström — real coordinates, never fractional. Producers may add further per-atom fields; consumers ignore what they don't understand. Biomolecular producers conventionally add `atom_name` (PDB cols 13-16, e.g. "CA"), `residue_name` (cols 18-20), `residue_seq` (cols 23-26), `chain_id` (col 22) and `b_factor` (cols 61-66); of these only `b_factor` is typed here, because the other four predate this schema and archives in the wild carry `residue_seq` both as an integer and as a string.

b_factor.description: Per-atom temperature factor / pLDDT-style confidence (PDB cols 61-66). The per-atom carrier is authoritative over the section-level `b_factors` array, because it cannot desynchronize from its own atom; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

Lattice3x3.description: Lattice as three ROW vectors in Ångström: row i is the lattice vector of axis i, paired with pbc[i].

StructurePayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `structure` section's `structure` member (conventionally `structure/structure.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. `pbc` is the normative carrier of per-axis periodicity; `dimensionality` is a derived convenience. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

pbc.description: Per-axis periodicity: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i]. REQUIRED when `lattice_vectors` is a non-null array; absent means a molecule ([false, false, false]). All eight patterns are legal — the periodic axes need NOT be the leading ones.

lattice_vectors.description: REQUIRED (non-null) when any pbc[i] is true; null or absent for a molecule. For every axis i with pbc[i] false, row i is non-physical bookkeeping — producers keep the matrix full-rank 3x3 so integrals and symmetry finders always see a 3-D lattice. Such a row is not a cell edge: a consumer MUST NOT draw it, replicate along it, or read it as a vacuum extent.

dimensionality.description: Derived count of periodic axes: equal to the number of true entries in `pbc`. Optional, and MUST agree when present. It carries no axis identity — a consumer MUST NOT infer WHICH axes are periodic from it.

allOf.$comment: A non-null lattice means the producer is describing a cell, so `pbc` must say which of its axes are periodic.
Conversely, a periodic axis needs the lattice vector that spans it.
dimensionality == sum(pbc), enumerated over 0..3 because JSON Schema counts matching items with minContains/maxContains rather than summing them.

BiomoleculeResidue.description: One residue of a biomolecular `structure` section. `atom_indices` are 0-based indices into the `structure` member payload's `atoms` array. Residues are listed in chain order — the order a consumer draws a ribbon in — not sorted by `seq`, because insertion codes and non-monotonic numbering are both legal and sorting would silently reorder them. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

seq.description: Residue sequence number (PDB cols 23-26). Not unique across a solvated system: PDB numbering is four columns wide and wraps at 9999, so a consumer MUST NOT use it as a global key.

chain.description: Chain id this residue belongs to; matches an entry of the section's `chains` when that is present.

atom_indices.description: 0-based indices into the structure payload's `atoms` array.

BiomoleculeSecondaryStructure.description: One inclusive secondary-structure range on one chain. A producer knows things a consumer cannot infer from CA geometry alone (alpha vs pi vs 3-10 helix, beta bridge vs sheet), so a consumer that also has its own geometric assignment MUST prefer these ranges where they are supplied; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

start_seq.description: First residue `seq` of the range, inclusive.

end_seq.description: Last residue `seq` of the range, inclusive.

SectionStructure.description: Atoms plus an optional cell. The `structure` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/StructurePayload` and the optional `bonds` member's by `#/$defs/BondsPayload`; because they are archive members rather than manifest content, a validator checks them separately from manifest.json; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds) and § 6 (Validation semantics). The optional biomolecule fields (`chains`, `residues`, `secondary_structure`, `b_factors`) sit on this section object rather than in the payload, and are independently optional: a structure carrying none of them is a valid plain structure, and a consumer that does not understand them ignores them. So do the optional fields of the species' chemical identity (`charge`, `multiplicity`, `name`, `smiles`, `inchi`, `inchikey`; the generic `label` is its compound label); see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

chains.description: Chain ids present in this structure, in the order a consumer should present them. OPTIONAL and additive.

residues.description: Residue decomposition of the structure, in chain order. OPTIONAL and additive. A consumer that can also derive residues from per-atom fields MUST prefer these when present.

secondary_structure.description: Per-chain secondary-structure ranges. OPTIONAL and additive; takes precedence over a consumer's own geometric assignment.

b_factors.description: One temperature factor per atom, parallel to the `structure` payload's `atoms` order. OPTIONAL and additive. A consumer MUST ignore the array entirely when its length differs from the atom count, rather than assigning a partial mapping; and per-atom `StructureAtom.b_factor`, where present, wins over this array.

charge.description: Net charge of the species whose atoms the `structure` payload holds, in units of the elementary charge. Absent states nothing (not neutral). With the payload's atomic numbers it gives the electron count, which must not be negative; in an archive with one `structure` section it must equal `provenance.charge` when both are present. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

multiplicity.description: Spin multiplicity 2S+1 of the species. With `charge`, multiplicity − 1 must not exceed the electron count and must have its parity; in an archive with one `structure` section it must equal `provenance.multiplicity` when both are present. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

name.description: Name of the species, e.g. 'ethanol'. The generic `label` is the short label a scheme shows, such as a compound number. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

smiles.description: SMILES of the species, hydrogens implied or explicit. It names the species as a whole and implies no atom order. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

inchi.description: InChI of the species, standard ('InChI=1S/…') or not. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

inchikey.description: InChIKey of the species. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

VolumeGridPayload.description: The JSON payload named by the `grid` member of every volume.* section and of a `basis.ao` section, and by the `volume_grid` member of a `reaction.path` section (conventionally `volumes/<section id>_grid.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The grid is point-centred: data index (i, j, k) lies at origin + i·v_i + j·v_j + k·v_k, so the data holds exactly `shape` points. Along an axis a that `periodic` marks, the grid samples one period of the cell of its structure: voxel_vectors[a] × (shape[a] − 1) spans lattice vector a when `includes_endpoint` is true (the default, cube style: the last plane repeats the first), and voxel_vectors[a] × shape[a] spans it when `includes_endpoint` is false (CHGCAR style); validators check the span. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

origin.description: Cartesian position of grid point (0, 0, 0), in bohr.

voxel_vectors.description: The step vectors v_i, v_j, v_k, in bohr: row n is the displacement between neighbouring points along data axis n. Non-zero off-diagonal components describe a non-orthogonal grid.

shape.description: Number of points [nx, ny, nz] along the three spatial data axes. It equals the shape of the section's 3-D `data` member, the leading three dimensions of a `volume.vector` or `volume.complex` `data` member, or the trailing three dimensions of a `volume.series` `data` member or of a `reaction.path` section's `frame_volumes` member.

periodic.description: Per-axis periodicity of the sampled field: periodic[a] true means the field repeats with lattice vector a of the grid's structure along data axis a, so a consumer may tile or wrap the grid along it. Absent means [false, false, false], a finite box. An axis may be periodic only where the structure's `pbc` is true, and voxel_vectors[a] must then span lattice vector a as `includes_endpoint` says; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

includes_endpoint.description: Whether the points along a periodic axis include the endpoint of the period. true (the default, cube-file style): the last plane is the image of the first, shape[a] − 1 steps span one period, and a consumer that tiles or wraps the grid MUST drop the duplicated plane. false (CHGCAR style): shape[a] distinct planes span one period, exclusive of the endpoint. It matters only on periodic axes; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

structure_ref.description: Id of the `structure` section whose cell the grid samples. It must name a section of kind `structure` in the archive. The section-level `structure_ref` takes precedence when both are present; with neither, the archive's only `structure` section is the grid's structure. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

units.description: Optional declaration of units: each key names a field of this payload or the role of a member of the section, each value a unit name. `origin` and `voxel_vectors` are fixed to `bohr`, and a declaration restates that; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

SectionVolumeGeneric.description: Generic scalar field — escape hatch for any volumetric kind that doesn't map onto density/orbital/spin/elf/difference. Structurally identical: grid + data. Producers should prefer a more specific kind when one fits.

SectionVolumeDifference.description: Difference density (or any difference scalar field). Structurally identical to volume.density; carries optional references to the two operand sections used to compute it. Sign convention: data = a - b.

operand_a.description: Section id of the minuend (the 'a' in a - b). Must reference a section that exists in this archive.

operand_b.description: Section id of the subtrahend (the 'b' in a - b). Must reference a section that exists in this archive.

SectionVolumePotential.description: Electrostatic potential grid — identical member structure to volume.density (grid + data). Data is in hartree/e (atomic units of potential). Specified in QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

SectionVolumeRDG.description: Reduced density gradient for NCI analysis — identical member structure to volume.density (grid + data). Data is dimensionless. Specified in QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

SectionVolumeLaplacian.description: Laplacian of the electron density, ∇²ρ, in e/bohr⁵: negative where charge concentrates, positive where it is depleted. Identical member structure to volume.density (grid + 3-D data). The vocabulary has no unit name for e/bohr⁵, so the grid does not declare `units.data` for it. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

SectionVolumeVector.description: A Cartesian vector field on a grid, such as a density gradient, an electric field or a current density: `data` is [nx, ny, nz, 3] with the x, y and z components on the last axis, in the Cartesian frame of the grid `origin`. Its unit is that of the field, which the grid declares as `units.data` when the vocabulary names it. The section field `component` is not used. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

SectionVolumeComplex.description: A complex scalar field on a grid, such as a complex orbital or a Bloch function at one k-point: `data` is [nx, ny, nz, 2] with the last axis [re, im]. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

SectionVolumeSeries.description: A series of n scalar fields on one grid, indexed by time, trajectory frame, electronic state or another quantity: `data` is [n, nx, ny, nz], slab s holding the field at the axis value `axis.values[s]`, and the required `axis` member says what the leading axis is. It supersedes, without deprecating, the `frame_volumes` + `volume_grid` members of a `reaction.path` section. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

VolumeSeriesAxisPayload.description: The JSON payload named by the `axis` member of a `volume.series` section (conventionally `volumes/<section id>_axis.json`): what indexes the leading axis of the section's `data` member, one entry per slab. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

kind.description: What indexes the slabs: `time` (the values are times), `frame` (0-based frame indices of the trajectory or reaction path named by `trajectory_ref`), `state` (electronic states, the values being state indices or energies) or `custom` (anything else, which `labels` describe).

values.description: The axis value of each slab, in slab order. It has n entries, n being the leading extent of `data`, which validators check.

units.description: Unit of `values`, a unit name. Absent means the values are pure numbers (`dimensionless`), as frame and state indices are; a time axis should declare its unit (`fs` or `ps`).

labels.description: Display label of each slab, n entries, e.g. "S1" for an excited state.

trajectory_ref.description: Id of the `trajectory` or `reaction.path` section whose frames the slabs belong to; the frame indices of a `frame` axis index its `coords`. It must name a section of one of those two kinds.

allOf.$comment: A frame axis counts frames, so its values are 0-based frame indices.

AtomChargeBinary.description: A per-atom scalar array: float64, shape [n_atoms]. Used by the scalar roles of an `atom_properties` section and by a scalar `custom.<name>` role. Specified in QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

AtomVectorBinary.description: A per-atom Cartesian vector array: float64, shape [n_atoms, 3]. Used by the vector roles `magnetic_moment` and `force_eh_bohr` of an `atom_properties` section and by a vector `custom.<name>` role. Specified in QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

AtomPropertyMetaEntry.description: The description of one `custom.<name>` role in the `meta` member of an `atom_properties` section. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

units.description: The unit of the role's values, spelled as in QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) where that gives a spelling; `dimensionless` for a pure number.

description.description: What the quantity is, including any sign convention.

kind.description: `scalar` for a float64 [n_atoms] member, `vector` for a float64 [n_atoms, 3] member.

AtomPropertiesMetaPayload.description: The JSON payload of the `meta` member of an `atom_properties` section: a map from the name of a `custom.<name>` role to its description. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only entries named by a `custom.<name>` role and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

SectionAtomProperties.description: Per-atom analysis results. The member roles are the one canonical role list: the scalar roles `mulliken_charge`, `loewdin_charge`, `hirshfeld_charge`, `iao_charge`, `spin_population`, `cm5_charge`, `chelpg_charge`, `resp_charge`, `esp_charge`, `nbo_charge`, `mbis_charge`, `bader_charge`, `ddec_charge`, `valence`, `bonded_valence`, `fukui_plus`, `fukui_minus`, `fukui_zero`, `dual_descriptor`, `atomic_energy_eh`, `atomic_volume_bohr3`, `nmr_shielding_iso_ppm`, each float64 [n_atoms], and the vector roles `magnetic_moment` and `force_eh_bohr`, each float64 [n_atoms, 3]. A section carries one or more of them, plus any number of `custom.<name>` roles (scalar or vector), which are allowed only together with a `meta` member that describes each of them. Specified in QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

TrajectoryCoords.description: Cartesian positions of every atom in every frame, [n_frames, n_atoms, 3], in Angstrom. float64, or float32 when the section's metadata sets `precision` to "float32"; that the dtype agrees with `precision` is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

TrajectoryFrameVectors.description: One 3-vector per atom per frame, float64 [n_frames, n_atoms, 3], in the atom and frame order of `coords`: the `velocities` (Angstrom/fs) and `gradient` (hartree/bohr) members of a trajectory or reaction path. That n_frames and n_atoms equal the extents of `coords` is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

TrajectoryFrameScalars.description: One number per frame, float64 [n_frames], in the frame order of `coords`: the `times` (fs), `energies` (hartree), `cell_volumes` (Angstrom^3) and `temperatures` (kelvin) members of a trajectory, and the `times` and `energies` of a reaction path. That n_frames equals the leading extent of `coords` is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

TrajectoryLattice.description: The cell of a periodic trajectory, float64, in the structure convention: each [3, 3] matrix holds the lattice vectors as ROWS (row i is the lattice vector of axis i, paired with metadata.pbc[i]), in Angstrom, exactly as `structure.lattice_vectors`. Shape [3, 3] when every frame shares one cell, or [n_frames, 3, 3] with one cell per frame (variable-cell and NPT runs). This is NOT the convention of the `lattice` member of a reaction path (columns, bohr); QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) states both. A trajectory that carries this member MUST carry metadata.pbc. That n_frames equals the leading extent of `coords` is checked by validators. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

SectionTrajectory.description: A sequence of frames of one set of atoms: an optimization, an IRC, a scan, a NEB or a molecular-dynamics run. `metadata` names the atoms and `coords` holds the positions; the optional members add per-frame data: the cell (`lattice`, rows in Angstrom), `velocities`, the energy `gradient` (the forces are its negative), `times`, `energies`, `cell_volumes` and `temperatures`. Every per-frame member has the leading extent of `coords`. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

velocities.description: Velocity of every atom in every frame, [n_frames, n_atoms, 3], in Angstrom/fs.

gradient.description: Energy gradient dE/dR of every atom in every frame, [n_frames, n_atoms, 3], in hartree/bohr, as the gradient member of a forces section: the forces are its negative.

times.description: Simulation time of each frame, in fs. When absent and metadata.timestep_fs is present, frame k is at k * timestep_fs.

energies.description: Energy of each frame, in hartree; the binary form of metadata.energies, preferred for long runs. When both are present they MUST agree within 1e-10 hartree.

cell_volumes.description: Cell volume of each frame, in Angstrom^3.

temperatures.description: Instantaneous temperature of each frame, in kelvin.

TrajectoryAtom.description: Identity of one atom in the `atoms` list of a trajectory-family metadata payload. Positions live in the section's binary members, not here; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

TrajectoryMetadataCommon.description: The keys that the metadata payloads of a `trajectory` (TrajectoryMetadataPayload) and of a `reaction.path` (ReactionPathMetadataPayload) share; each of those definitions extends this one. It names the atoms, in the atom order of `coords`, through at least one of `symbols`, `atomic_numbers` and `atoms`; per-frame arrays are in frame order. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

atoms.description: Atom identities as objects, an alternative to `symbols` and `atomic_numbers`. When more than one of the three is present they MUST describe the same atoms.

n_frames.description: Number of frames; equals the leading dimension of `coords`.

energies.description: Energy of each frame, in Hartree. When the section also carries the binary `energies` member, the two MUST agree within 1e-10 hartree.

kind.description: What produced the frames: a geometry optimization, an intrinsic reaction coordinate, molecular dynamics, a nudged elastic band, a coordinate scan (relaxed or rigid), or something else.

pbc.description: Per-axis periodicity of the frames: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i], as in the `structure` payload. Absent means the frames are molecular. For a `trajectory` it is REQUIRED when the section carries a `lattice` member, and a true entry requires that member.

ensemble.description: Thermodynamic ensemble of a molecular-dynamics run: constant N, V, E; N, V, T; N, p, T; N, p, H; or another.

timestep_fs.description: Time between consecutive frames, in fs. When the section has no `times` member, frame k is at k * timestep_fs.

precision.description: Floating-point precision of the `coords` member; absent means float64. It MUST agree with that member's dtype: float32 coords require "float32" here.

units.description: Optional declaration of units: each key names a field of this payload or the role of a member of the section, each value a unit name. The units are fixed, and a declaration restates them: `energies` is `hartree`, `coords` is `angstrom`, and `times` and `timestep_fs` are `fs`; the `velocities` (Angstrom/fs) and `gradient` (hartree/bohr) members have no unit name and are not declared. See QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

TrajectoryMetadataPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `trajectory` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. It carries the keys of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, which a `reaction.path` metadata payload shares (ReactionPathMetadataPayload), and fixes the units of the members only a trajectory has. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

units.description: The `units` declaration of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, which also fixes the trajectory-only members: `lattice` is `angstrom` (rows, the structure convention), `cell_volumes` is `a3` and `temperatures` is `kelvin`; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

SectionReactionPath.description: Self-contained reaction path: frames + per-frame energies + waypoint annotations identifying reactant / transition state / intermediate / product frames. Binary layout matches `trajectory` so the same readers can decode coords. Optional per-frame volumetric data (electron density / an orbital morphing along the path) may be attached via the `frame_volumes` (4D: [n_emitted_frames, nx, ny, nz]) + `volume_grid` members; the metadata then carries `volume_frame_index` (which path frame each emitted slab belongs to, for decimation), `volume_label`, and optional `volume_isovalue`. Readers that don't understand these members ignore them. These two members are the older form of a `volume.series` section whose `axis` has kind `frame` and names the path, which producers should prefer; both stay valid. The optional `velocities`, `gradient`, `times` and `energies` members carry per-frame data with the shapes and units they have in a trajectory, and the optional `lattice` member (columns, bohr) marks the path periodic; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

velocities.description: Velocity of every atom in every frame, [n_frames, n_atoms, 3], in Angstrom/fs, as for a trajectory.

gradient.description: Energy gradient dE/dR of every atom in every frame, [n_frames, n_atoms, 3], in hartree/bohr; the forces are its negative.

times.description: Time of each frame, in fs, as for a trajectory.

energies.description: Energy of each frame, in hartree; the binary form of metadata.energies. When both are present they MUST agree within 1e-10 hartree.

ReactionWaypoint.description: One annotated frame of a reaction path, an item of the `waypoints` list of a `reaction.path` metadata payload or of a `reaction.waypoints` payload. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

frame_index.description: 0-based index of the annotated frame: into the section's own `coords` for `reaction.path`, into the `coords` of the trajectory named by `trajectory_ref` for `reaction.waypoints`.

kind.description: Role of the frame on the path; `point` marks any other annotated frame.

energy_eh.description: Energy of the frame, in Hartree.

ReactionPathMetadataPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `reaction.path` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. It carries every key of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, the keys it shares with a `trajectory` metadata payload, plus waypoint annotations, an optional reaction coordinate, and the keys that describe the optional per-frame volumes (the `frame_volumes` and `volume_grid` members). Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

reaction_coordinate.description: Value of the reaction coordinate at each frame, in frame order: the abscissa of an energy profile.

reaction_coordinate_label.description: Display label of the reaction coordinate.

dim.description: Number of periodic dimensions, shared by every frame of a periodic path.

dim_per_frame.description: Number of periodic dimensions of each frame, for a path whose frames differ; used instead of `dim`.

volume_frame_index.description: For each slab of the `frame_volumes` member, in order, the 0-based path frame it belongs to, so that volumes can be emitted for a subset of the frames. One entry per slab.

volume_label.description: Display label of the per-frame volumes, e.g. "density".

volume_isovalue.description: Suggested isovalue for the per-frame volumes, in the unit of their data.

units.description: The `units` declaration of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, which also fixes the `lattice` member of a periodic path to `bohr` (columns, unlike the `lattice` of a trajectory); see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

ReactionPathLattice.description: Per-frame lattice vectors as a binary member, specified in QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations). Each lattice is a 3x3 matrix with columns = a, b, c, in bohr. Shape is either [3, 3] when every frame shares the same lattice (the fixed-cell common case — recommended) or [n_frames, 3, 3] when frames carry per-frame lattices (forward-compat with variable-cell scans). When this member is absent the reaction.path is a molecular trajectory and renderers must draw no cell. Presence of this member — not the manifest version — is how a consumer detects a periodic reaction path.

SectionScanSurface.description: 2D relaxed-scan energy surface: two driven internal coordinates (axis_a x axis_b) with the relaxed energy at each grid node. `energies` is a 2D binary array [nA, nB]; `axis_a` / `axis_b` are the 1D coordinate values (bohr for bonds, radians for angles/dihedrals). The metadata carries per-axis label + unit. Optional `geometries` (4D-flattened [nA*nB, n_atoms, 3] in angstrom, row-major over (a, b)) lets a viewer show the relaxed structure at a clicked node.

ScanSurfaceAxis.description: One driven coordinate of a `scan.surface` section; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

unit.description: Unit of the coordinate values in the matching `axis_a` / `axis_b` binary member, e.g. "bohr" or "rad".

atoms.description: 0-based indices of the atoms that define the coordinate: two for a distance, three for an angle, four for a dihedral.

ScanSurfaceMetadataPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `scan.surface` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The structured axis descriptions `axis_a` and `axis_b` are preferred; the flat label keys are recognised alternatives, and when both forms are present the objects take precedence. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

axis_a.description: The first driven coordinate, along the rows of `energies`.

axis_b.description: The second driven coordinate, along the columns of `energies`.

atoms.description: Atom identities, in the atom order of the `geometries` member.

energy_unit.description: Unit of the `energies` member values; absent means Hartree.

units.description: Optional declaration of units: each key names a field of this payload or the role of a member of the section (`axis_a`, `axis_b`, `energies`, `geometries`), each value a unit name. A declared unit is the unit the values are stored in. When `units.energies` and `energy_unit`, or a `units` entry and an axis `unit`, are both present they MUST name the same unit; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

SectionReactionWaypoints.description: Lightweight waypoint annotations layered onto an existing `trajectory` section. Use this when the frames are already carried by a trajectory and you only want to label reactant/TS/intermediate/product frames without duplicating coords.

trajectory_ref.description: Section id of the trajectory section this annotation refers to. Must reference an existing section with kind 'trajectory' in this archive.

ReactionWaypointsPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `reaction.waypoints` section's `waypoints` member (conventionally `<section id>/waypoints.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

waypoints.description: Annotated frames of the trajectory named by the section's `trajectory_ref`.

reaction_coordinate.description: Value of the reaction coordinate at each frame of that trajectory, in frame order.

SectionReactionScheme.description: A reaction scheme: steps that relate `structure` sections as reactants, reagents and products, with the kind of arrow, the conditions and the yield. The `scheme` member's JSON payload is `#/$defs/ReactionSchemePayload`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

ReactionSchemePayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `reaction.scheme` section's `scheme` member (conventionally `<section id>/scheme.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it, and also checks that every participant names a `structure` section, that step ids are unique and that no structure occurs twice within one role of a step. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

steps.description: The steps of the scheme, in reading order.

ReactionStep.description: One step of a reaction scheme. Roles are chemical: `reactants` are consumed and `products` formed in the step's forward direction whatever the `arrow`, so for a retrosynthetic arrow the target is among the `products`. The key `energies` is reserved for a later revision. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

id.description: Identifier of the step, unique within the payload.

label.description: Display label of the step, e.g. 'a' or 'step 2'.

reagents.description: Species drawn at the arrow: reagents, catalysts, solvents drawn as structures.

arrow.description: The kind of arrow: 'forward' (reactants → products), 'equilibrium' (⇌), 'retrosynthetic' (products ⇒ reactants: target at the tail, precursors at the head) or 'resonance' (two resonance structures of one species, no reaction). Absent means 'forward'.

conditions.description: The text written at the arrow, one entry per line, in reading order.

yield_percent.description: Yield of the step's products, in percent.

yield_text.description: The yield as printed, e.g. '87%', '>95%' or 'quant.'.

ReactionParticipant.description: A species of a reaction step: the `structure` section that holds it and its stoichiometric coefficient. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

structure_ref.description: Id of the `structure` section of the species. It must name a section of kind `structure` in this archive.

coefficient.description: Stoichiometric coefficient of the species in the step; absent means 1.

hessian_ref.description: Optional id of the hessian section the modes were derived from; a validator checks that it names a hessian section. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

VibrationsMetadataPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `vibrations` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Per-mode arrays hold one entry per mode, in the mode order of `displacements`. An imaginary mode is written as a negative frequency whose magnitude is the imaginary wavenumber. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

frequencies.description: Harmonic wavenumber of each mode, in cm⁻¹; negative for an imaginary mode.

ir_intensities.description: IR intensity of each mode, in km·mol⁻¹.

raman_activities.description: Raman scattering activity of each mode, in Å⁴·amu⁻¹.

reduced_masses.description: Reduced mass of each mode, in amu.

force_constants.description: Force constant of each mode, in mdyn·Å⁻¹.

imaginary.description: Per-mode flag, true for an imaginary mode. When present it MUST agree with the sign of `frequencies`.

n_modes.description: Number of modes; equals the leading dimension of `displacements`.

symbols.description: Element symbol of each atom, in the atom order of `displacements`.

atoms.description: The reference geometry: one atom per atom of `displacements`, in the same order, with Cartesian positions in Ångström.

SectionSpectraIR.description: One-dimensional infrared spectrum. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/SpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

SpectrumPayload.description: The JSON payload named by the `spectrum` member of a one-dimensional spectrum section: `spectra.ir`, `spectra.raman`, `spectra.uvvis`, `spectra.ecd`, `spectra.vcd` or `spectra.generic`. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Typed-open: the fields below are typed and the root stays open. `frequencies` carries the x axis in the unit QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) gives the kind, unless `x_units` declares another; the name is kept for every kind, including those whose x values are energies. `frequencies`, `intensities` and, when present, `x` MUST have the same length. JSON Schema cannot express that rule, so a validator checks it separately; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra) and § 6 (Validation semantics).

frequencies.description: The x value of every point or line. Unit: the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions), or `x_units` when present.

intensities.description: The y value of each entry of `frequencies`, in the same order. Unit: the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions), or `y_units` when present.

x.description: Optional alias of `frequencies` under a quantity-neutral name: the same values in the same order. `frequencies` stays REQUIRED; a consumer may read either.

x_units.description: Unit name of `frequencies` and `x`. Absent means the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

y_units.description: Unit name of `intensities`. Absent means the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

peaks.description: Annotated peaks, in the units of `frequencies` and `intensities`.

broadening.description: The line shape the producer applied to turn discrete lines into an envelope, or recommends a consumer to apply.

fwhm.description: Full width at half maximum of the line shape.

units.description: Unit name of `fwhm`. Absent means the unit of the x axis.

temperature_k.description: Temperature the spectrum refers to, in kelvin.

raman.description: Raman-specific data, meaningful in a `spectra.raman` payload.

depolarization_ratios.description: Depolarization ratio of each line, in the order of `frequencies`.

uvvis.description: UV-Vis-specific data, meaningful in a `spectra.uvvis` payload.

x_axis.description: The x quantity the producer recommends for display: excitation energy in eV or wavelength in nm. It does not change the stored values, whose unit `frequencies` and `x_units` define.

states_ref.description: Id of the `excited_states` section whose states the peaks name: every `peaks[].assignment.state_index` is then the `index` of a state of that section. It must name a section of kind `excited_states` in this archive; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

SpectrumPeak.description: One annotated peak of a `SpectrumPayload`. `x` and `width` are in the unit of the payload's `frequencies`, `y` in the unit of its `intensities`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

width.description: Full width at half maximum of the peak.

assignment.description: What the peak arises from. `mode_index` is a 0-based index into the modes of the archive's `vibrations` section; `state_index` identifies the electronic state the transition reaches: the `index` of a state of the `excited_states` section that the payload's `states_ref` names, or, without `states_ref`, as the producer numbers its states.

SectionSpectraRaman.description: One-dimensional Raman spectrum. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/SpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

SectionSpectraUVVis.description: One-dimensional UV-Vis absorption spectrum. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/SpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

SectionSpectraECD.description: One-dimensional electronic circular dichroism spectrum. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/SpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

SectionSpectraVCD.description: One-dimensional vibrational circular dichroism spectrum. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/SpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

SectionSpectraNMR.description: Nuclear magnetic resonance parameters. The payload is a single object-shaped `spectrum` JSON member rather than a frequency/intensity pair, specified by `#/$defs/NmrSpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

NmrSpectrumPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `spectra.nmr` section's `spectrum` member: per-nucleus chemical shifts, shielding tensors and spin-spin couplings rather than a frequency/intensity pair. Permissive: the known fields are typed, every object stays open, and a later revision may tighten the definition. Shifts and shieldings are in ppm, couplings in Hz. See QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

solvent.description: Solvent or solvation model, when one was used.

isotropic_shift_ppm.description: Isotropic chemical shift relative to `reference`, in ppm.

shielding_tensors.description: Full shielding tensors, one entry per nucleus.

tensor.description: Shielding tensor in ppm: three rows in the Cartesian frame of the structure.

isotropic_ppm.description: Isotropic shielding, one third of the trace, in ppm.

j_couplings.description: Indirect spin-spin couplings, one entry per atom pair.

SectionSpectraEPR.description: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR / ESR) parameters. Like spectra.nmr, the payload is a single object-shaped `spectrum` JSON member rather than a frequency/intensity pair; it carries the g-tensor, per-nucleus hyperfine (A) tensors, and the zero-field-splitting (D) tensor. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/EprSpectrumPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

EprSpectrumPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `spectra.epr` section's `spectrum` member: the g-tensor, per-nucleus hyperfine (A) tensors and the zero-field-splitting (D) tensor. Permissive: the known fields are typed, every object stays open, and a later revision may tighten the definition. Units are fixed: g-values are dimensionless, hyperfine and zero-field-splitting parameters are in MHz. See QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

matrix.description: Full g-tensor, dimensionless: three rows in the Cartesian frame of the structure.

isotropic.description: Isotropic g-value, one third of the trace.

hyperfine.description: Hyperfine couplings, one entry per magnetic nucleus.

a_tensor_mhz.description: Full hyperfine tensor in MHz: three rows in the Cartesian frame of the structure.

d_mhz.description: Axial zero-field-splitting parameter D, in MHz.

e_mhz.description: Rhombic zero-field-splitting parameter E, in MHz.

tensor_mhz.description: Full zero-field-splitting tensor in MHz: three rows in the Cartesian frame of the structure.

SectionSpectraGeneric.description: One-dimensional spectrum of a kind QVF does not name. The `spectrum` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/SpectrumPayload`; producers SHOULD declare its `x_units` and `y_units`. See QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

MoCoefficientsBinary.description: MO coefficients of a `wavefunction.gto` section, float64, one row per MO: [n_mo, n_ao] when real, [n_mo, n_ao, 2] with the last axis (real, imaginary) when the `mo_metadata` payload says `complex: true`. A `generalized` wavefunction doubles the AO axis to 2 n_ao, all α components first. That the rank matches `complex` is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

SectionWavefunctionGTO.description: Atom-centered Gaussian basis + MO coefficients. Renderer-friendly: a re-sampling viewer can evaluate any orbital on its own grid (Molden-style). Complex coefficients are stored as float64 [n_mo, n_ao, 2] with last axis [real, imag]. Optional AO-basis matrices: the `overlap` matrix, with which a consumer verifies the normalization contract of QVF spec Appendix A.1, and the one-particle density matrices `density_matrix` (with `mo_coefficients`) or `density_matrix_alpha` + `density_matrix_beta` (with the α and β coefficients). See QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

WavefunctionAoMatrix.description: An optional AO-basis matrix of a `wavefunction.gto` section, float64 [n_ao, n_ao], rows and columns in the AO order of the `basis` payload (QVF spec Appendix A.2): the `overlap` matrix of the contracted AOs as QVF spec Appendix A.1 defines them (dimensionless), or a one-particle density matrix in the AO basis (`density_matrix` the spin-summed total, `density_matrix_alpha` and `density_matrix_beta` one spin each), so that the trace of a density matrix times the overlap is the number of electrons it describes. That n_ao matches the basis, and that the density members pair with the coefficient members, are checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

BasisShell.description: One contracted shell of a `basis` payload. It contributes 2l+1 (spherical) or (l+1)(l+2)/2 (Cartesian) AOs, ordered as in QVF spec Appendix A.2. `exponents` and `coefficients` are parallel, one entry per primitive, and MUST have the same length; JSON Schema cannot express that rule, so this definition does not check it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

center.description: 0-based index of the atom the shell sits on, in the `atoms` of the `structure` section named by the payload's `structure_ref`.

l.description: Angular momentum of the shell (0 = s, 1 = p, 2 = d, …).

coefficients.description: Contraction coefficients, one per exponent, applying to primitives normalized as QVF spec Appendix A.1 prescribes.

pure.description: true = spherical harmonics, false = Cartesian. Overrides the payload-level `pure` for this shell.

BasisEcpProjector.description: One radial function of an effective core potential, in the conventional semi-local form U(r) = Σ_i c_i r^(n_i − 2) exp(−α_i r²), with r in bohr and U in hartree: parallel arrays with one entry per term i, which MUST have the same length (JSON Schema cannot express that rule, so this definition does not check it). With `local: true` it is the local part of the centre's potential, which acts on every angular momentum; otherwise it is the semi-local channel of angular momentum `l`, which acts through the projector onto `l`. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

l.description: Angular momentum of the channel. For the local part (`local: true`) it is the conventional label L of that part, which is greater than the `l` of every semi-local channel of the centre.

exponents.description: Gaussian exponents α_i of the terms, in bohr⁻².

coefficients.description: Coefficients c_i of the terms, in hartree · bohr^(2 − n_i), so that every term is an energy in hartree.

powers.description: Radial powers n_i of the terms: term i is c_i r^(n_i − 2) exp(−α_i r²), so n_i = 2 is a plain Gaussian and n_i = 0 carries r^(−2).

local.description: true: this radial function is the local part U_L(r) of the centre's potential, which acts on every angular momentum; a centre has at most one, and its `l` is the highest on the centre. false or absent: a semi-local channel, which multiplies the projector onto angular momentum `l`. As in the usual tabulations, a semi-local channel of a centre with a local part holds the difference U_l(r) − U_L(r).

BasisEcpCentre.description: The effective core potential on one atom of a `basis` payload: it replaces the `n_core_electrons` innermost electrons of that atom, which the wavefunction therefore does not describe. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

center.description: 0-based index of the atom, as for a shell's `center`.

n_core_electrons.description: Number of electrons the potential replaces on this atom: the wavefunction describes the remaining Z − n_core_electrons of the atom's electrons.

projectors.description: The radial functions of the potential: at most one local part and the semi-local channels. Absent: the potential is named by `label` and its core count only, and a consumer that needs the potential itself cannot evaluate it.

BasisPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.gto` section's `basis` member (conventionally `<section id>/basis.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The AO order is the concatenation of the shells in array order, each in the in-shell order of QVF spec Appendix A.2. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

structure_ref.description: Id of the `structure` section whose atoms the shell `center` indices refer to.

pure.description: Angular type of every shell without its own `pure`: true = spherical harmonics, false = Cartesian. Absent means true.

n_ao.description: Number of AOs: the sum over the shells of 2l+1 (spherical) or (l+1)(l+2)/2 (Cartesian). It equals the AO dimension of the MO coefficient members.

shells.description: The contracted shells, in AO order.

ecp.description: Effective core potentials, at most one per atom (no two entries share a `center`); see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

n_electrons.description: Number of electrons the wavefunction describes: the sum of the atomic numbers, minus the `n_core_electrons` of every `ecp` entry, minus the charge. When present it equals the sum of the `mo_metadata` occupations over both spin channels (within 1e-6) and `provenance.n_electrons` when that is present; validators check both, which JSON Schema cannot express.

MoSpinChannel.description: The orbitals of one spin channel of an unrestricted `mo_metadata` payload: per-MO arrays in the row order of the matching `mo_coefficients_alpha` or `mo_coefficients_beta` member. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

n_mo.description: Number of MOs in the channel; equals the row count of its coefficient member.

energies.description: Orbital energy of each MO, in Hartree.

occupations.description: Occupation of each MO, in electrons (0 to 1 in a spin channel), or a squared singular-value transition weight when occupation_semantics is transition_weight. For unrestricted NTOs, the nonnegative weights are in non-increasing order, match the paired section per spin, and both spins together sum to 1 for a normalized state; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

symmetry_labels.description: Irreducible-representation label of each MO of the channel, parallel to its `energies`; validators check the length.

MoMetadataPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.gto` section's `mo_metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/mo_metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. `spin` selects one of two shapes. `unrestricted` carries an `alpha` and a `beta` object, matching the `mo_coefficients_alpha` and `mo_coefficients_beta` members, and no top-level per-MO arrays. Every other `spin` value carries one set of orbitals, matching `mo_coefficients`, with `energies` and `occupations` at the top level and no `alpha` or `beta`. Per-MO arrays are in the row order of the coefficient member. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. The deprecated keys `iao_charges`, `excitation_index` and `excitation_energy_ev` remain valid so that archives which carry them keep validating; producers write their canonical carriers instead; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

spin.description: `restricted`: one set of spatial orbitals shared by both spins. `unrestricted`: separate α and β sets. `restricted_open`: one set of spatial orbitals, singly or doubly occupied, in the restricted shape. `generalized`: one set of two-component spin orbitals that mix α and β, in the restricted shape with the AO axis of `mo_coefficients` doubled to 2 n_ao (the α components of the n_ao AOs, then their β components); it requires `complex: true`. See QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

orbital_kind.description: What the orbitals are; absent means `canonical`. `canonical`: eigenfunctions of the converged Fock or Kohn-Sham operator. `natural`: natural orbitals. `localized`: localized orbitals of an unnamed method. `nto`: natural transition orbitals. `nbo`: natural bond orbitals. `iao`, `ibo`: intrinsic atomic and bond orbitals. `boys`, `pipek_mezey`: Foster-Boys and Pipek-Mezey localized orbitals. `custom`: anything else.

n_ao.description: Number of AOs; equals the `basis` payload's `n_ao`.

n_mo.description: Number of MOs; equals the row count of `mo_coefficients`.

energies.description: Orbital energy of each MO, in Hartree.

occupations.description: Occupation of each MO: electrons per orbital, or a transition weight when `occupation_semantics` says so.

symmetry_labels.description: Irreducible-representation label of each MO, parallel to `energies`; validators check the length.

alpha.description: The α orbitals of an unrestricted wavefunction; for NTOs they pair by row with the α channel of the other section, independently of β (QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto)).

beta.description: The β orbitals of an unrestricted wavefunction; for NTOs they pair by row with the β channel of the other section, independently of α (QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto)).

occupation_semantics.description: Meaning of the `occupations` numbers: electrons per orbital (`electron_occupation`, the meaning when absent) or the weights of natural transition orbitals (`transition_weight`).

k_point.description: Crystal momentum of the orbitals, in fractional coordinates of the reciprocal lattice; absent or [0, 0, 0] means the Γ point.

complex.description: true when every coefficient member is complex, float64 [n_mo, n_ao, 2] (2 n_ao for `generalized`) with the last axis (real, imaginary); absent or false means real [n_mo, n_ao]. Validators check the rank of the coefficient members against it.

coefficient_encoding.description: Alternative spelling of `complex`: `real` means false, `complex_split_last_axis` means true. When both are present they MUST agree.

coefficient_components.description: Order of the last axis of complex coefficients; when present it is ["real", "imag"].

state_ref.description: Reference to the electronic state the orbitals describe, for state-specific orbitals. For natural transition orbitals (`orbital_kind` nto) it is the id of the `excited_states` section, and `state_index` names the state; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

state_index.description: The `index` of the state that the orbitals describe, in the `excited_states` section that `state_ref` names.

nto_role.description: Which half of a state's natural transition orbitals the section holds: `hole`, the occupied-space orbitals, or `particle`, the virtual-space orbitals. Row k of the hole section pairs with row k of the particle section of the same state; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

localization_method.description: Name of the method that localized the orbitals.

localization_reference_basis.description: Name of the minimal reference basis of free-atom AOs from which the intrinsic atomic orbitals were constructed, e.g. 'minao' (IAO and IBO localization; Knizia, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2013, 9, 4834). The IAOs, and the IAO charges and IBOs derived from them, depend on this choice; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

atom_populations.description: [n_mo, n_atoms]: the fraction of each localized orbital on each atom; each row sums to 1.

centroids_bohr.description: [n_mo, 3]: the centroid of each localized orbital, in bohr.

n_centres.description: Number of atoms each localized orbital is centred on.

iao_charges.description: Deprecated; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). The IAO partial charge of each atom, in e. Producers SHOULD NOT write it: the canonical carrier is the `iao_charge` member of an `atom_properties` section. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid.

excitation_index.description: Deprecated; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). The excited state that natural transition orbitals describe, by the producer's own numbering. Producers SHOULD NOT write it: the canonical carrier is `state_index`, the state's `index` in the `excited_states` section that `state_ref` names. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid.

excitation_energy_ev.description: Deprecated; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). The excitation energy, in eV, of the state that natural transition orbitals describe. Producers SHOULD NOT write it: the canonical carrier is the `excitation_energy` of the state that `state_index` names in the `excited_states` section that `state_ref` names. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid.

allOf.$comment: Canonical unrestricted NTOs (nto_role present) are two sections per state, paired per spin; cross-member rules are checked by validators (QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto)).
The two shapes: separate alpha/beta channels for unrestricted, one top-level orbital set otherwise.
A generalized (two-component) wavefunction is complex; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

SectionWavefunctionBloch.description: Provisional kind. The k-resolved Bloch orbitals of a periodic system over the atom-centred Gaussian basis of its cell: complex MO coefficients at every k-point of a set, for one or two spin channels, with their energies and occupations. The Bloch functions are phi_mu,k(r) = N^(-1/2) sum_T exp(+i k.T) chi_mu(r - T) over the lattice translations T, with k in fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates and the AO order and primitive normalization of QVF spec Appendix A. The structure named by the section-level structure_ref, else by basis.structure_ref, must have at least one periodic axis; validators check that and the agreement of the member shapes. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

BlochMoCoefficients.description: Complex MO coefficients, float64 [n_k, n_spin, n_mo, n_ao, 2]: element [k, s, m, mu, :] is the (real, imaginary) pair of the coefficient of Bloch function mu at k-point k in MO m of spin channel s (0 is alpha, 1 is beta). Axis 0 follows the kpoints member, axis 3 the AO order of the basis. That the extents agree with the other members is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

BlochEnergies.description: Orbital energies, float64 [n_k, n_spin, n_mo], in hartree, in the order of the first three axes of mo_coefficients. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

BlochOccupations.description: Orbital occupations, float64 [n_k, n_spin, n_mo], in electrons per orbital at each k-point, not weighted by the k-point weights: 0 to 2 when n_spin is 1, 0 to 1 when it is 2. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

BlochKpointsPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.bloch` section's `kpoints` member: the k-points the orbitals are given at, in the order of axis 0 of mo_coefficients, energies and occupations. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. That the arrays have one entry per k-point and that the weights sum to 1 within 1e-6 is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

kpoints.description: Every k-point, in fractional coordinates of the reciprocal lattice (k = k1 b1 + k2 b2 + k3 b3, so k.T = 2 pi (k1 n1 + k2 n2 + k3 n3) for the translation T = n1 a1 + n2 a2 + n3 a3).

weights.description: Integration weight of each k-point, one per entry of `kpoints`, summing to 1 within 1e-6. Absent when the k-points are not an integration set, such as points along a path.

labels.description: One label per k-point, parallel to `kpoints`, such as a high-symmetry name; an empty string marks an unlabelled point.

mesh.description: Dimensions [n1, n2, n3] of the uniform mesh the k-points were taken from, when they were; the k-points are its points, or the irreducible subset of them that the weights account for.

shift.description: Fractional reciprocal-lattice position of mesh point (0, 0, 0). Absent means a Gamma-centred mesh.

time_reversal.description: True when the set was reduced with time-reversal symmetry: the orbitals at -k are the complex conjugates of those at k, and the weight of k includes that of -k. Absent means false.

units.description: Optional map from a field name of this payload to the unit name of its values. The fields are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) and the payload table; a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `kpoints`, `weights` and `shift` are `dimensionless`.

BlochMoMetadataPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.bloch` section's `mo_metadata` member: the orbital set the binary members carry. Per-orbital energies and occupations are the binary members `energies` and `occupations`, not fields of this payload. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

spin.description: `restricted`: one set of spatial orbitals shared by both spins (n_spin 1). `unrestricted`: separate alpha and beta sets (n_spin 2).

n_spin.description: Number of spin channels; equals axis 1 of mo_coefficients, energies and occupations.

n_mo.description: Number of MOs at each k-point and spin; equals axis 2 of mo_coefficients, energies and occupations.

n_ao.description: Number of AOs; equals axis 3 of mo_coefficients and the basis payload's n_ao.

orbital_kind.description: What the orbitals are, with the values and meanings of the wavefunction.gto mo_metadata field of the same name; absent means `canonical`.

complex.description: Always true: mo_coefficients carries (real, imaginary) pairs in its last axis.

k_point_convention.description: How the kpoints member states k: `fractional`, in fractional coordinates of the reciprocal lattice. The only value in v1.

n_mo_per_k.description: Number of orbitals that are defined at each k-point, one entry per k-point, each at most n_mo, for a producer whose orbital count differs between k-points (canonical orthogonalisation that removes a different number of near-linear-dependent directions at each k). Orbitals n_mo_per_k[k] to n_mo - 1 at k-point k are padding, with zero coefficients and zero occupations, and consumers ignore them. Absent means n_mo at every k-point.

fermi_energy.description: Fermi level of the calculation, on the absolute scale of `energies`.

units.description: Optional map from the role of a member of the section to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `energies` is `hartree`.

SectionBands.description: Band structure — eigenvalues along a k-path, with optional Mulliken character projections (fat bands).

BandsProjections.description: Fat-band weights of a `bands` section: float64 [n_spin, n_k, n_bands, n_channels], or the legacy rank-3 form [n_k, n_bands, n_channels], which means n_spin = 1. n_spin, n_k and n_bands are those of `eigenvalues`; channel c is entry c of the kpath `channels` list. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

BandsOccupations.description: Occupation of each band state of a `bands` section: float64 [n_spin, n_k, n_bands], the shape of `eigenvalues`, in electrons per state (not weighted by k-point weights). See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

KpathSegment.description: One straight segment of a band-structure path, listed in path order. Indices count points along the path axis (axis 1 of bands `eigenvalues`, axis 0 of phonon `frequencies`) from 0. When `start` is absent it is the previous segment's `end` (0 for the first segment), so consecutive segments share their boundary point; when `end` is absent it is start + n_points - 1. A path with a jump gives the segment after the jump an explicit `start`. Keys beginning with x_ are a vendor escape. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

start.description: Index of the segment's first point.

end.description: Index of the segment's last point (inclusive).

n_points.description: Number of points on the segment, both ends included.

label_start.description: High-symmetry label of the first point (e.g. 'G' or 'Γ'); may be empty.

label_end.description: High-symmetry label of the last point; may be empty.

k_start.description: Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of the first point.

k_end.description: Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of the last point.

KpathPayload.description: The JSON payload named by a `bands` section's `kpath` member: the path the eigenvalues are sampled on, the Fermi level, and the fat-band channels. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. No field is required. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

kpoints.description: Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of every k-point along the path, in the order of eigenvalues axis 1 (n_kpoints entries).

labels.description: One label per k-point along the path, parallel to `kpoints` and eigenvalues axis 1; an empty string marks an unlabelled point.

segments.description: The straight segments of the path, in path order.

fermi.description: Fermi level in eV, on the absolute scale of `eigenvalues` (eigenvalues are not shifted by it).

fermi_energy_ev.description: The Fermi level under the name the DOS kinds use. When both are present it equals `fermi`.

spinor.description: True when the bands come from a two-component (spin-orbit) calculation: n_spin is then 1 and each band is one spinor state.

n_spin.description: Number of spin channels; equals eigenvalues axis 0.

n_kpoints.description: Number of k-points along the path; equals eigenvalues axis 1.

n_bands.description: Number of bands; equals eigenvalues axis 2.

channels.description: Fat-band channels, one per last-axis slice of `projections`. A string is shorthand for a channel object carrying only that `label`.

title.description: Display title of the band structure.

units.description: Optional map from a field name of this payload, or the role of a member of the section, to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `fermi`, `fermi_energy_ev` and `eigenvalues` are `ev`.

kind.description: Informational echo of the section kind.

version.description: Informational producer label for the payload layout; consumers do not rely on it.

reciprocal_space.description: Informational; k-points are always reciprocal-space coordinates.

SectionDOSTotal.description: Total density of states on an energy grid. Its metadata rides as optional fields on the section object (`n_spin`, `smearing`, `smearing_type`, `fermi_energy_ev`, `n_electrons`), not as members. Specified in QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

n_spin.description: Number of spin channels: 1 (spin-unpolarized) or 2 (spin-polarized). OPTIONAL.

smearing.description: Width of the broadening applied to the DOS, in eV. OPTIONAL.

smearing_type.description: Name of the broadening function, for example "gaussian". OPTIONAL; free text in v1.

n_electrons.description: Number of electrons; may be fractional. OPTIONAL.

SectionDOSProjected.description: Projected density of states on an energy grid. Its metadata rides as optional fields on the section object, as for dos.total, plus `channels`, which labels the projection rows. Specified in QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

n_spin.description: Number of spin channels: 1 (spin-unpolarized) or 2 (spin-polarized). OPTIONAL.

smearing.description: Width of the broadening applied to the DOS, in eV. OPTIONAL.

smearing_type.description: Name of the broadening function, for example "gaussian". OPTIONAL; free text in v1.

n_electrons.description: Number of electrons; may be fractional. OPTIONAL.

channels.description: One label object per projection row, in row order. OPTIONAL. Every item field is optional, and items may carry further fields.

atom.description: 0-based index of the projected atom in the structure section.

l.description: Angular momentum quantum number of the projection.

m.description: Magnetic quantum number of the projection.

DOSProjectedProjections.description: Projected DOS of a `dos.projected` section: [n_spin, n_channels, n_points], or the legacy rank-2 form [n_channels, n_points], which means n_spin = 1. n_points is the length of `energies`; channel c is entry c of the section's `channels` list. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

DosChannel.description: One projection channel of a DOS, fat-band or phonon projection: the atom, shell and component a slice of the projections belongs to. Typed-open: the fields below are typed and further keys are allowed. An absent field means the channel sums over that quantity (no `atom`: all atoms; no `l`: all shells; no `m`: all components of the shell). See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

atom.description: 0-based index of the atom in the structure section.

l.description: Angular momentum of the shell (0 = s, 1 = p, ...).

m.description: Component within a spherical shell, -l..l, as in QVF spec Appendix A.2.
